items.title: آنچه گذشت؛ محسن رضایی: هیچ مذاکره‌ای با آمریکا در جریان نیست
items.summary: دبیر شورای عالی امنیت ملی ایران می‌گوید در حال حاضر هیچ مذاکره‌ای با آمریکا در جریان نیست. محسن رضایی گفته است که پیش از بازگشایی تنگه هرمز و ازسرگیری مذاکرات، ایالات متحده باید هفت شرط تعیین‌شده در تفاهم اسلام‌آباد را بپذیرد و به آن‌ عمل کند. دبیر شورای‌عالی امنیت ملی گزارش‌های منتشرشده درباره برنامه‌ریزی برای دیدار با معاون رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا در قطر را «کاملاً نادرست و بی‌اساس» خوانده است.

items.title: محسن رضایی: اگر آمریکا حمله کند پایگاه‌های دوردستش را هم هدف قرار می‌دهیم
items.summary: محسن رضایی، دبیر شورای عالی امنیت ملی ایران، گفته کشورش اجازه خروج «حتی یک ذره» اورانیوم از خاکش را نخواهد داد و همزمان در صورت حمله مجدد نظامی آمریکا به این کشور، ایران اهداف فرامنطقه‌ای را هم در واکنش نظامی خود قرار خواهد داد. همزمان محمدباقر قالیباف تاکید کرده که تنگه هرمز به وضعیت قبل از جنگ باز نخواهد گشت. مسعود پزشکیان هم که برای شرکت در اجلاس اقلیمی به ترکیه رفته است گفته: «هیچ قدرتی حق ندارد به نام امنیت، بنیادهای حیات بر زمین را با خطر مواجه سازد.»

items.summary: پیش‌بینی می‌شود که جمهوری‌خواهان سنا یک شکست خیره‌کننده دیگر را متحمل شوند، این بار در می‌سی‌سی‌پی قرمز قابل اعتماد. به گزارش آسوشیتدپرس، پیش بینی می شود که سناتور فعلی سیندی هاید اسمیت، رئیس خانم، در رقابتی که تا هفته های پایانی اکتبر به بن بست رسیده بود، نامزد خود را برای دومین دوره کامل در مجلس سنای ایالات متحده برای اسکات کولوم، دادستان منطقه ای ایالتی، از دست بدهد. بیش از یک هفته پس از روز انتخابات، آسوشیتدپرس این رقابت را به نفع کولوم در روز چهارشنبه اعلام کرد و در تلنگری دیگر، قدرت دموکرات ها در مجلس سنای ایالات متحده را به 55 در مقابل 44 کرسی جمهوری خواهان رساند. شبکه سوروس در تلاش برای برگرداندن کرسی سنا، می سی سی پی قرمز عمیق را هدف قرار می دهد، دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا، پشت سر او و خرید آگهی هفت رقمی و لحظه آخری توسط صندوق رهبری سنا، یک کمیته اقدام سیاسی که نزدیک به سنا است، تجمع کرد.
items.summary_original: Senate Republicans are projected to suffer yet another stunning setback, this time in reliably red Mississippi. Incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., is projected to lose her bid for a second full term in the U.S. Senate to state District Attorney Scott Colom in a race, according to The Associated Press, that until the final weeks of October, was deadlocked. More than a week after Election Day, the AP called the razor-thin race in favor of Colom on Wednesday, pushing the Democrats' hold on the U.S. Senate to 55 seats to the Republicans' 44 in another flip. SOROS NETWORK TARGETS DEEP-RED MISSISSIPPI IN BID TO FLIP SENATE SEAT President Donald Trump rallied behind her and a seven-figure, last-minute ad buy by the Senate Leadership Fund, a political action committee closely tied to Senate Majority Leader John Thune , R-S.D., were not enough to stop Colom’s momentum. CHUCK SCHUMER AFTER SWEEPING DEMOCRATIC MIDTERM VICTORIES: 'I'LL BE RE-ELECTED AS MAJORITY LEADER' Her loss to Colom, who she previously blocked for a district court seat under the Biden administration years ago, comes after both parties rallied big names and resources in an effort to prevent a nightmare scenario for Republicans. This is a breaking story; check back later for updates.

"All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times," the soldier said. The instruction came around 12:30 p.m., after Trump had left the ceremony. items.summary_original: Iran claims it struck a small Omani island in the Strait of Hormuz , targeting oil tanker navigation infrastructure as CENTCOM maintains its blockade of Iranian ports and protects commercial shipping from Iranian attacks along the southern route. Three sources also confirmed to Reuters Wednesday that navigation systems and communications equipment on Didamar Island, also known as Little Quoin Island, had been attacked, raising concerns about the vulnerability of maritime infrastructure used to maintain oil shipments through the Gulf. Iran's semiofficial Fars News Agency reported that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy targeted the island, alleging the systems were being used to help vessels transit the strait without Tehran's authorization. WHITE HOUSE SILENT ON IRAN-OMAN HORMUZ PLAN TEHRAN SAYS WOULD BAN US WARSHIPS Iranian state television also claimed that personnel and equipment on the island "were helping the flow of oil smuggling by the enemy," with the IRGC maintaining it had carried out the strikes, Reuters reported. Video published by Reuters showed smoke rising near the rocky outcrop. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) said it identified the attack as occurring Nov. 8, before Iranian state media claimed responsibility on Nov. 10. ISW also questioned the extent of the reported damage, noting that commercial vessels continued using the southern route after the attack. items.summary_original: Unruly protesters set fires, smashed storefronts and launched fireworks at riot police across parts of Spain on Wednesday as a massive nationwide strike over soaring housing costs disrupted transportation and businesses. Violent scenes unfolded in Barcelona, where some demonstrators vandalized stores along the city's popular Paseo de Gracia shopping boulevard, set small bonfires and launched fireworks at officers arriving in riot gear and armored vehicles, according to The Associated Press . The violence erupted after a largely peaceful march as Spain experienced its first general strike in 14 years, with workers demanding relief from skyrocketing rents and the rising cost of living. TRAVELERS MAY FACE MAJOR DISRUPTIONS AS STRIKES THREATEN AIRPORTS AND POPULAR ATTRACTIONS Housing activists claimed 400,000 people marched through Barcelona, while city officials estimated attendance at 55,000. Government officials reported another 120,000 demonstrators gathered in Madrid despite heavy rain, the AP reported. The nationwide walkout disrupted public transportation, forced some businesses to close and blocked major roads. Police made arrests across the country, while officers used pepper spray against demonstrators in Madrid, according to the AP. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump's former personal attorney, Alina Habba Mildon, has lost a four-year contract worth more than $50 million to serve as general counsel for a company founded by the daughter of a Venezuelan billionaire Trump pardoned earlier this year, according to The New York Times. Concord Partners, a Florida-based company founded by Isabela Herrera, daughter of Venezuelan banker Julio Herrera Velutini, terminated Habba Mildon’s contract after President Donald Trump urged the Herrera family to stop paying her, The Philadelphia Inquirer reported Wednesday. A source familiar with the matter confirmed the termination to Fox News Digital. TRUMP SIGNS PARDONS FOR ALASKA DIESEL MECHANICS ONSTAGE DURING RALLY TOUTING MAJOR ENERGY DEALS Concord Partners cited a "failure to perform duties" in a Nov. 4 termination letter obtained by The New York Times. Trump pardoned Venezuelan banker Julio Herrera Velutini Jan. 15, 2026, just two weeks after Habba Mildon began working for the company founded by his daughter. Herrera faced federal bribery charges tied to an alleged scheme involving Puerto Rico’s governor and struck a plea deal accepting a misdemeanor campaign finance violation in August 2025. The firing came just days after Trump publicly blasted Habba Mildon’s $50 million arrangement as excessive and said he did not want her to receive the money. "There’s no decision on what’s next," Scalise said on Wednesday. "I’ve got to get through these next few weeks, and then we have a lot of decisions to make about what's life going to look like in the minority. But I sure still have a great passion for this country." JIM JORDAN THROWS HAT IN RING FOR HOUSE MINORITY LEADER AS GOP PICKS UP PIECES AFTER BLUE WAVE Scalise’s answer follows a loss to Rep. Jim Jordan , R-Ohio, in a bid to become the party’s new minority leader. His defeat now forces Scalise to decide whether he intends to retire or remain on Capitol Hill as a rank-and-file member of the minority as Democrats retake control of the House in January. For now, Scalise stressed that he remains focused on securing GOP priorities before the new year. "There’s a lot more for us to do. We have a few weeks left in the lame duck [session] and, frankly, a few big, big issues ahead. I want to see us do as much as we possibly can while we still have this majority," Scalise said. items.summary_original: Four grizzly bears have been linked through DNA evidence to a deadly attack on a mother and daughter in British Columbia , prompting Canadian wildlife officers to kill all four animals, officials announced Tuesday. The British Columbia Conservation Officer Service said forensic testing conclusively linked an adult female grizzly and her three offspring to the deaths of Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter, Selah Reed, 20, near Bella Coola. The bears were captured over the weekend and killed in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines to protect public safety, according to a Nov. 10 statement from the agency. BODY OF MISSING HIKER DISCOVERED OFF TRAIL AS INVESTIGATORS PROBE RARE DEADLY BEAR ENCOUNTER Investigators determined that the encounter likely involved predatory behavior, although officials did not elaborate on how the attack unfolded. "This was a heartbreaking event for the families, the Nuxalk Nation and the Bella Coola community. We hope the efforts of everyone who responded, along with these findings, bring some measure of closure," said Insp. Jeff Tyre in a news briefing. More than a dozen conservation officers participated in the response, helping recover the victims, collect evidence and locate the bears while working in difficult terrain and weather conditions. items.title_original: Russian Ambassador to US Alexander Darchiev dies suddenly at 66
items.summary: وزارت امور خارجه روسیه اعلام کرد، الکساندر دارچیف 66 ساله سفیر روسیه در آمریکا روز چهارشنبه به طور ناگهانی درگذشت. در بیانیه روسیه که به انگلیسی ترجمه شده است، آمده است: «رهبری و کارکنان وزارت خارجه روسیه با اندوه عمیق گزارش می دهند که در 11 نوامبر در سن 66 سالگی، الکساندر نیکیتیچ دارچیف، سفیر فوق العاده و تام الاختیار فدراسیون روسیه در ایالات متحده آمریکا به طور ناگهانی درگذشت. "یک دیپلمات برجسته، یک رهبر باتجربه، همکار مهربان و مربی این زندگی را ترک کرده است. A.N. دارچیف، یک آمریکایی حرفه ای و درخشان، در یکی از حیاتی ترین و پرمخاطره ترین جبهه های سیاست خارجی روسیه خدمت کرده است." ما عمیق ترین و صمیمانه ترین تسلیت خود را به خانواده و عزیزان الکسان ابراز می کنیم
items.summary_original: Russia's Ambassador to the United States Alexander Darchiev, 66, died suddenly Wednesday, the Russian Foreign Ministry announced. "The leadership and staff of the Russian Foreign Ministry report with deep sorrow that on Nov. 11, at the age of 66, the Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Russian Federation to the United States of America, Alexander Nikitich Darchiev, passed away suddenly," Russia's statement , as translated to English, said. "A distinguished diplomat, experienced leader, kind colleague, and mentor has departed this life. A consummate professional and brilliant Americanist, A.N. Darchiev served on one of the most critical and demanding fronts of Russian foreign policy." "We express our deepest and most sincere condolences to the family and loved ones of Alexander Nikitich Darchiev," the statement added. "The cherished memory of our untimely departed colleague will forever remain in our hearts." Fox News confirmed the death came in Russia and not the U.S. MELANIA TRUMP HAILS OLESHKY CEASEFIRE AS POTENTIAL ‘SPARK’ FOR PROGRESS AMID UKRAINE-RUSSIA WAR Russia's Vladimir Putin appointed Darchiev, a veteran diplomat known in the past for his public denunciations of the West, as ambassador to Washington in March 2025 to lead a rapprochement with the Trump administration that has rattled Ukraine, the European Union and NATO. His death comes less than a week after a White House news conference hailing a temporary ceasefire in Ukrainian territory occupied

He highlighted the 1983 Iran-backed bombing of the U.S. Marine Corps barracks in Beirut and argued that Iran has been at war with the U.S. for decades. "America did not start a war with Iran. Iran has been waging war on America since 1979. They should have been taken care of a long time ago," Trump said. We won. Now the question is when we want to end. We must have a total victory. Not a 93% victory. It's going to be total," he continued. Trump noted that of the roughly seven months of conflict, "only a few weeks were active fighting," but he acknowledged the casualties America sustained. "We lost 18 beautiful souls," Trump said. items.summary_original: The share of military veterans in Congress is projected to fall to its lowest level in decades in the incoming 120th Congress, but while overall veteran representation continues a long-term decline, the partisan composition of the freshman class marks a sharp contrast. Democrats are bringing roughly three times as many first-time veteran members as Republicans, and they are catching up among House members overall. Still, as America marks Veterans Day, the numbers show the institutional voice of military service in the legislative branch is heading toward its lowest watermark in modern history. AFTER GOP'S BRUTAL MIDTERMS, ‘CHUCK NORRIS OF FLORIDA POLITICS’ TELLS PARTY TO 'GET UP AND FIGHT' Analysis from With Honor Action and Military Times indicates veterans will hold roughly 15% of seats when the new Congress convenes in January, down from about 19% in the outgoing body and well below the 27% recorded in 2001 before the war on terror began. That comes despite a record number of veterans running in 2026, according to the analysis. In January 2025, there were just 28 Democrats compared to 72 Republicans, according to Military Times . Among the 79 projected for the 120th Congress, the partisan gap is closing to 33 Democrats and 46 Republicans. items.summary_original: Israel's newly elected parliament was sworn in Tuesday, marking the beginning of a political transition that could end Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's long tenure in power. Despite the opposition's parliamentary gains, the country remains without a new government, and negotiations to form one face significant obstacles. At the center of those negotiations is former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, who was tasked by President Isaac Herzog on Sunday with assembling Israel's next governing coalition after 67 lawmakers recommended him for the position, compared with 46 who supported Netanyahu. Although Eisenkot's Yashar party won 21 seats in the Oct. 27 election , he is working closely with former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, whose B'Yachad party, formed with former Prime Minister Yair Lapid, secured another 12 seats. NETANYAHU FACES COALITION SHOWDOWN AS RIVALS MANEUVER TO FORM ISRAEL'S NEXT GOVERNMENT The two parties have not merged, but their cooperation effectively gives Eisenkot the negotiating backing of 33 lawmakers — more than Netanyahu's Likud, which remains the largest individual party in the Knesset with 27 seats. A source with knowledge of discussions within the bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu told Fox News Digital that Bennett has decided to act as a political kingmaker, supporting Eisenkot's leadership bid rather than seeking the premiership himself. items.summary_original: FIRST ON FOX: Some House Democrats are leaving the door open to additional articles of impeachment against War Secretary Pete Hegseth over his handling of military aid to Ukraine, according to lawmakers who spoke with Fox News Digital after a failed impeachment effort led by Republican Rep. Thomas Massie. But a conservative legal expert suggested the renewed impeachment push may be less about removing Hegseth from office than discouraging conservatives from serving in future Republican administrations. Massie, R-Ky., told Fox News Digital that while he could not substantiate allegations that Hegseth improperly withheld military assistance to Ukraine, he believes Democrats will investigate the matter and potentially introduce additional articles of impeachment when they take control of Congress in January. "I believe [Democrats] may use some of the same articles of impeachment when they're in the majority, but I also believe there are gonna be some other articles of impeachment based on hearings and committees," Massie told Fox News Digital. "I think the Democrats will do that." Ilhan Omar , D-Minn., told Fox News Digital on Tuesday she was never informed by federal agencies of the grounds on which she is being investigated — even claiming she isn’t sure how many probes into her there are. "No, no," she said when asked if she had been told exactly the basis for the investigations. There are two known ongoing federal probes into the Somali-born congresswoman — the first, confirmed by sources to Fox News Digital, is the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) looking into whether her immigration paperwork was fraudulently filled out by herself or her father; and the second is investigating her financial disclosures discrepancies and was confirmed publicly by U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro. ILHAN OMAR'S TURBULENT WEEK EXPLAINED: THE DUELING PROBES THAT THREW THE SOMALI-BORN PROGRESSIVE INTO CHAOS On Omar’s first day back on Capitol Hill following the investigations, she told Fox News Digital she doesn't know if DHS and the Department of Justice (DOJ) are each investigating her independently. "I’m not sure," Omar said. "You probably have more details on that." The congresswoman's feigned innocence on the matter came after she had a two-hour meeting with her lawyers at her Capitol Hill office on Tuesday. Sanders was complimentary of Schumer, but said at a news conference on Tuesday that he believes "the time is now" for change in Democratic leadership. "I personally have known Chuck Schumer for over 30 years, and I like Chuck. [There’s] nobody who works harder than Chuck Schumer. But in my view, the time is now for change, and I will not be supporting Chuck to be re-elected as the Democratic leader," Sanders said at a news conference. Elissa Slotkin , D-Mich., joined Sanders at the Tuesday news conference and said she also will not be supporting Schumer . Neither has backed a specific candidate to replace Schumer, however. "I am not actively seeking this job. I am seeking change," Slotkin said. "I’ve been very consistent for a very long time that we need a new generation of leadership … It’s important to demonstrate that we’ve heard what people want from this last election." I thought his message that he put out the day after the election was abhorrent and, frankly, smacked of the kind of thing you’d read in 1932 Germany," Fine, who is himself Jewish, said in an interview with Fox Now. "He’s out in my book," he added. "He blamed the Jews for losing the election." It also underscores tensions in the GOP as the party wrestles with how to balance America-First principles with its alliance with Israel. items.summary_original: Minnesota Governor-elect Amy Klobuchar, who has positioned herself as a moderate during her years in Congress, is facing blowback over comments made shortly after the election suggesting she will push for gun control when she takes office. "The gun safety bill is going to get passed, and I am so excited to be working with the leaders on this, and it certainly should be one of our top priorities," Klobuchar said during a press conference. "I think that bill makes a lot of sense. I’m sure that we’ll make some changes … but the basics of that bill I hope will remain in place." The bill Klobuchar referenced is SF 4067, an omnibus gun-control package that passed the Minnesota Senate 34-33 earlier this year but has not received a House vote. The measure would prohibit federally licensed firearms dealers from selling certain semiautomatic military-style assault weapons, including AR-15s, as well as large-capacity magazines capable of holding more than 17 rounds. The legislation would allow current owners to keep the covered firearms and magazines, but require them to obtain an ownership certification from the state Bureau of Criminal Apprehension and renew that certification every three years. Knowingly possessing an uncertified weapon or magazine would be a gross misdemeanor, with a subsequent violation punishable as a felony. items.summary_original: DUBAI, United Arab Emirates — In a historic house near Dubai Creek, a small gallery commemorating the six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust stands alongside collections exploring Islamic civilization, Emirati heritage and the history of Palestine and the Holy Land. The Holocaust exhibition at the privately owned Crossroads of Civilizations Museum is among the first permanent displays of its kind in the Arab world. Opened in May 2021, less than a year after the UAE normalized relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords, it has become a symbol of the Emirates' approach to religious coexistence. During a recent visit to the museum, Fox News Digital saw displays documenting Nazi persecution, including a life-size image of the boy from the famous Warsaw Ghetto photograph, his hands raised in surrender. The gallery also tells the stories of Muslims who rescued Jews during the Holocaust, including Egyptian physician Mohammed Helmy, who sheltered Jews from Nazi persecution in Berlin. US-BACKED ISRAEL-MOROCCO DEAL DEEPENS ABRAHAM ACCORDS AMID GROWING REGIONAL THREATS But the story behind the exhibition is as personal as the objects it preserves. In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, museum founder Ahmed Obaid Al Mansoori, a former member of the UAE's Federal National Council, explained that his passion for collecting historical artifacts began in childhood, when he inherited family manuscripts and objects from his grandparents. items.summary_original: FIRST ON FOX: As America celebrates 250 years of independence this year, three conservative Supreme Court justices are warning that preserving the nation's founding freedoms for future generations depends on Americans understanding their history, embracing civic education and actively participating in their system of government. Justices Brett Kavanaugh, Neil Gorsuch and Amy Coney Barrett each implored Americans to familiarize themselves with their system of government and the history behind it to ensure that the nation’s legacy is preserved. Though the three conservative justices were united in their call for civic education, they each approached the topic differently in a series of interviews filmed by the Federalist Society and obtained by Fox News Digital. The videos come ahead of the Federalist Society's 2026 National Lawyers Convention this week, which spotlights "250 Years of American Exceptionalism." Gorsuch, for instance, struck a distinctly religious tone. Shortly after winning, Thune declared that he and the Senate GOP were "committed to being here to do whatever it takes to get as much done as we can." "That means extending the calendar here, the number of days we're here, the number of hours we're here, the number of votes we may end up taking," Thune said. "But we are going to finish this legislative session strong." items.summary_original: Rep. Madeleine Dean, D-Pa., is reportedly mulling a U.S. Senate bid , a move which could mean challenging Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., who would need to seek re-election in 2028 if he wants to pursue a second term. "I’m going to be considering it," Dean said in an interview with Politico published Tuesday. Dean expressed disappointment with Fetterman's performance as a senator. GAZA-BORN DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST LAUNCHES PRIMARY BID AGAINST SEN JOHN FETTERMAN "I have been concerned about, really, two things, which is his family and his health … and am very disappointed in his activity as a senator and in his votes," she noted, according to Politico. Dean's campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's comment request on Wednesday. BITTER FETTERMAN-EL-SAYED FEUD THREATENS TO COMPLICATE SCHUMER'S SENATE UNITY PUSH The congresswoman, who has served in the House since early 2019, just won re-election to a fifth term. Last year, a report quoted Dean as saying there was "no way" that she would mount a bid to challenge Fetterman. FETTERMAN PLAYS POLITICAL MAVERICK, BUT HIS VOTING RECORD TELLS ANOTHER STORY But she strongly criticized Fetterman after he recorded a video that played during the GOP midterm convention earlier this year. "To me, that was a very sad stunt, that he would stand there aligning himself with the most corrupt president of our lifetime, if not the most corrupt president in history. I have said I hope John comes back to the Democratic fold," she said.

items.summary_original: Fifteen years after Dakota Meyer left the Marine Corps , the Medal of Honor recipient decided to put the uniform back on — becoming the first with the award to ever reenlist. Meyer was 36. He had fought in Afghanistan, struggled with the transition home from war and spent years building a life outside the military. But he said the desire to serve never went away. "Every day after I took that uniform off, that desire to serve didn't just end because my commitment to the country did," Meyer told Fox News Digital in an interview ahead of Veterans Day . AMERICAN WAR HERO DETAILS DIRE LIVING CONDITIONS US TROOPS FACE AS HEGSETH TAPS HIM TO 'FIX' IT Meyer rejects the idea that receiving the Medal of Honor meant he had already done enough. "I think sometimes it's looked at as you've done your part, and I am wholeheartedly against that," he said. "I believe that the only time you've done your part is when you've done all that you can." For Meyer, Veterans Day is a reminder that service does not necessarily end when someone leaves the military. "Sometimes we look at the veteran title as it is something that represents something we've done," Meyer said. "And it's not. It's something that we are doing, and it is something that we can continue to do." items.summary_original: A Marine veteran from a small North Carolina town spent 16 years fighting to build a national memorial honoring the Americans who served in Desert Shield and Desert Storm — overcoming congressional setbacks, years of bureaucratic hurdles and a lengthy battle over its location, all while refusing to use taxpayer money to get it done. "I'm just an average everyday American," Scott Stump told Fox News Digital. "I just felt like something had to be done to correct what I felt was a historical oversight." What began as one veteran's determination to ensure the sacrifices of the 1990-1991 Gulf War generation were not forgotten became a 16-year undertaking that culminated in the Oct. 24, 2026, opening of the Desert Shield and Desert Storm Memorial on the National Mall . Stump, who spearheaded the effort with a team of veteran volunteers, said he insisted from the beginning that the project be built without U.S. taxpayer funding, even as it required years of congressional action, federal approvals and financial support from donors. items.summary: مارکوین مولین، وزیر امنیت داخلی آمریکا روز سه شنبه پیامی صریح در مورد سیاست مهاجرتی ارائه کرد و وعده "عدم تغییر" را پس از انتخابات میان دوره ای که ضربه سختی به حزب جمهوری خواه وارد کرد، داد. مولین این اظهارات را در حین حضور در برنامه "زاویه اینگراهام" شبکه فاکس نیوز بیان کرد، جایی که لورا اینگراهام مجری برنامه، رئیس جمهور دونالد ترامپ را مطرح کرد که به جمهوری خواهان پیشنهاد همکاری با دموکرات ها را داد. مولین گفت: «عفو هرگز روی میز نخواهد بود. کاخ سفید پس از خشم ترامپ از طریق معامله غیرقانونی بیگانگان با دموکرات ها دو برابر شد. ما اصلاً سرعتمان را کاهش نداده‌ایم. ما کاری را که انجام می‌دهیم با رفتن به دنبال بدترین‌ها، با گرفتن قاتلان و رپ اولویت‌بندی کرده‌ایم.
items.summary_original: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin delivered a blunt message on immigration policy Tuesday, promising "zero change" following the midterm elections that dealt a crushing blow to the Republican Party. Mullin made the remarks during an appearance on Fox News' "The Ingraham Angle," where host Laura Ingraham brought up President Donald Trump suggesting Republicans work with Democrats. "Amnesty will never be on the table," Mullin said. WHITE HOUSE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER TRUMP ANGERS BASE BY FLOATING ILLEGAL ALIEN DEAL WITH DEMS He noted that the agency has been deporting roughly 3,600 individuals a day and has no plans to slow down. "We haven't slowed down at all. We've reprioritized what we're doing by going after the worst of the worst, by getting the murderers and the rapists and child predators and drug bankers and cartel members," he added. While Democrats secured majorities in both the House and Senate during the midterm elections, Mullin said Republicans cannot trust the opposing party to work with them. "You can't trust the Democrat Party we've been working with at all. You can't, because nothing's enough for them," he said. He also criticized the Democratic Party's leadership, pointing to the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) and accusing the group of wanting to "defund the country." "You got DSA that's running the Democrat Party right now. They want to defund my agency, the Department of Homeland Security," he said. BORDER DEM POISED TO WIELD ICE

items.summary_original: The U.S. Air Force abruptly relocated more than a dozen aircraft from RAF Mildenhall in eastern England amid an emerging security threat, U.S. officials confirmed Tuesday. The Wall Street Journal first reported the move, citing sources who said the threat originated in Iran. As U.S. officials assessed the threat's nature and urgency, commanders raised the base's security level to Force Protection Condition Charlie, the military's second-highest alert level, indicating a likely terrorist threat against personnel or facilities. IRAN HAS 'SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED' EFFORTS TO TARGET AMERICANS ABROAD, US INTELLIGENCE MEMO WARNS Flight-tracking data and open-source analysts with the Military Air Tracking Alliance identified 13 U.S. aircraft leaving the base late Monday, the Associated Press said. Nine Boeing KC-135 Stratotankers were moved to airfields in Scotland, Germany and Spain. Three CV-22B Ospreys were relocated to nearby RAF Lakenheath, which has hardened aircraft shelters. A U.S. official told The Associated Press the moves were precautionary, noting that some aircraft were on rotational deployments while others were permanently stationed in the United Kingdom . IRAN UNDER SCRUTINY AFTER PLOT FOILED NEAR UK BASE USED BY US MILITARY The move marks the second major relocation of U.S. military aircraft from Britain in less than two months. items.summary_original: A 7-year-old girl with dual U.S. and Mexican citizenship was shot and killed during a Mexican security operation targeting an alleged cartel member, and her mother accused police officers aboard a helicopter of firing the deadly shot. Aranza Aidelany Pardo died Oct. 29 in Matamoros, a Mexican border city across from Brownsville, Texas. She was among six people killed during the operation and subsequent roadblocks erected by the Gulf Cartel, according to The Associated Press. Her mother, Claudia Pardo García, told the AP that gunfire from a Tamaulipas state police helicopter struck her daughter in the head. Pardo was also wounded in the leg. Mexican authorities are investigating three officers aboard the helicopter who remain on active duty, according to Tamaulipas Public Security Secretary Carlos Arturo Pancardo. EXCLUSIVE: INSIDE TRUMP'S CARTEL CRACKDOWN AS WHITE HOUSE OFFICIAL DETAILS PRESIDENT'S PRIVATE BRIEFINGS The operation resulted in the arrest of Axel Alfredo Cárdenas Rodríguez, also known as El Titán, the son of an alleged Gulf Cartel leader and nephew of the group's imprisoned founder, Osiel Cárdenas Guillén. Pardo told the AP that she, her husband and their five children were returning home when they encountered cartel roadblocks and took a rural shortcut. She said a police helicopter began following their vehicle before circling in front of it. Her husband exited with his hands raised to show officers they were a family, but gunfire erupted. items.summary_original: A senior U.S. Army soldier was arrested in England Tuesday on suspicion of espionage offenses related to Russia, according to U.K. police. The 41-year-old man, whose identity was not released, was detained as part of an investigation into suspected national security threats led by Counter Terrorism Policing , according to the Metropolitan Police. Officials said the arrest was carried out in coordination with the U.S. military and the FBI. "This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies," FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement. FBI OFFERS $200K REWARD FOR FORMER AIR FORCE INTELLIGENCE AGENT ACCUSED OF SPYING FOR IRAN The soldier was arrested near Gloucester, and police are currently searching two locations in the wider Gloucestershire area as part of the ongoing joint U.K.-U.S. investigation. Police said the man was detained under the National Security Act 2023 and remains in custody at a London police station. The investigation is ongoing and is being led by officers from the Counter Terrorism Policing team in London. JD VANCE پس از بازگشت به واشنگتن
items.summary_original: Iran's top security official, who reportedly received a letter from Vice President JD Vance about resuming peace talks, warned in a resurfaced interview that wartime negotiations with Tehran could drag on for decades, and during which both sides should "be prepared to fight." Mohsen Rezaei, a former commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), now serves as secretary of the Supreme National Security Council and acts as a key aide to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. He also helped shape Tehran's military strategy during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq War . That eight-year conflict ended after Iran's then-supreme leader, Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, accepted a U.N.-brokered cease-fire that he famously likened to drinking from a "poisoned chalice." JD VANCE RETURNS TO WASHINGTON AFTER 16 HOURS OF IRAN PEACE TALKS COLLAPSE IN PAKISTAN "Ceasefire means an unfinished war," Rezaei had said of the war in a 2006 interview with the Iranian publication Baztab. An English translation of the interview is preserved by George Washington University's National Security Archive . Asked whether both sides would remain in their positions and begin talks, Rezaei replied: "Yes. Negotiations can take 30 to 40 years and during that time Iran and Iraq should be prepared to fight." Two decades after suggesting negotiations could drag on for years, Washington has reportedly been seeking talks with Rezaei, a key power player in Iran’s current military leadership. items.summary: به گفته مقامات، شوهر یک مجری تلویزیون روز یکشنبه در پاکستان پس از اینکه جسد همسرش با شلیک گلوله به سرش پیدا شد، دستگیر شد. به گفته عظما زاهد بخاری، وزیر اطلاعات پنجاب، رابعه احسن، 41 ساله، ظاهراً در داخل خانه خود در راولپندی کشته شده است. احسن به عنوان مجری برنامه 92 نیوز مشغول به کار شد و در آنجا در کنار همکاران ارشد خود به عنوان یک روزنامه نگار متعهد شناخته شد. او همچنین به طور مکرر ویدیوهایی در مورد مسائل ملی در شبکه های اجتماعی منتشر می کرد. بخاری گفت که مقامات شوهر او را احسن طاهر خان شناسایی کردند که مدعی شد در خانه با سلاح گرم بازی می کرد که به طور تصادفی آن را تخلیه کرد. مجری محبوب تلویزیون، چهره‌های ستاره رسانه‌ای پس از محکومیت در پرونده عمده قاچاق مواد مخدر به دار آویخته شدند.
items.summary_original: The husband of a TV anchor was arrested in Pakistan Sunday after his wife was found dead with a gunshot wound to the head, according to officials. Rabiya Ahsan, 41, was allegedly killed inside her home in Rawalpindi, according to Punjab Information Minister Azma Zahid Bokhari. Ahsan worked as a program host for 92 News, where she established herself as a dedicated journalist alongside senior colleagues. She also frequently posted videos about national affairs on social media. Officials identified her husband as Ahsan Tahir Khan, who claimed he was playing with a firearm in the home when it accidentally discharged, Bokhari said. POPULAR TV HOST, MEDIA STAR FACES HANGING AFTER CONVICTION IN MAJOR SYNTHETIC DRUG TRAFFICKING CASE Khan reportedly works as a civil service officer at the Overseas Pakistanis Foundation, a government agency that supports citizens living abroad, according to local outlet The Express Tribune, citing police sources. Police are preparing to pursue a murder case against the suspect , according to the report. Rawalpindi police also confirmed in a post on X that a woman was killed in a Sunday shooting but did not immediately identify her. Authorities said officers seized the suspected weapon in connection with the husband's arrest. Ahsan's body was also transferred to a hospital for a postmortem examination. items.summary: امانوئل مکرون، رئیس‌جمهور فرانسه، در حالی که با تشدید آشفتگی‌های سیاسی و اقتصادی در داخل کشور دست و پنجه نرم می‌کند، برنامه‌های خود را برای حضور نظامی جدید اروپایی در لبنان ادامه می‌دهد، حتی در شرایطی که این ابتکار با مقاومت یکی از شرکای کلیدی اروپایی مواجه می‌شود و واشنگتن جایگزینی را در نظر می‌گیرد که ممکن است نیازی به نیرو نداشته باشد. مارکو روبیو، وزیر امور خارجه آمریکا تایید کرد که درباره آینده نیروی موقت سازمان ملل متحد در لبنان (یونیفیل) با مکرون صحبت کرده است و پیشنهاد می کند که مکانیسم نظارتی جایگزین می تواند غیرنظامی باشد تا نظامی. روبیو در اظهاراتی که روز سه شنبه منتشر شد گفت: "این نباید یک ماموریت نظامی باشد. می تواند یک ماموریت غیرنظامی باشد." روبیو توضیح داد که دولت به دنبال مکانیزمی معتبر برای راستی آزمایی ترتیباتی است که بر اساس آن نیروهای اسرائیلی عقب نشینی می کنند.
items.summary_original: French President Emmanuel Macron is pushing ahead with plans for a new European military presence in Lebanon while struggling with mounting political and economic turmoil at home, even as the initiative encounters resistance from a key European partner and Washington considers an alternative that may not require troops. Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed that he had discussed the future of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) with Macron, suggesting that a replacement monitoring mechanism could be civilian rather than military. "It doesn't have to be a military mission. It could be a civilian mission," Rubio said in remarks published Tuesday. Rubio explained that the administration is seeking a credible mechanism to verify arrangements under which Israeli forces withdraw from designated areas, the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) assume control and the Iran-backed terrorist group Hezbollah is prevented from returning. RUBIO ANNOUNCES FRAMEWORK DEAL BETWEEN ISRAEL AND LEBANON AS EXPERTS WARN IRAN WILL FIGHT TO SABOTAGE IT He suggested France could play a constructive role but emphasized that any arrangement would require agreement from both Lebanon and Israel. U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz also made clear that Washington has no intention of preserving the existing peacekeeping mission. items.summary: سرعت راه رفتن می‌تواند سرنخ‌هایی مهم درباره سلامت جسمی و شناختی افراد در اختیار ما بگذارد. پژوهش‌ها نشان داده‌اند که کندتر راه رفتن فقط نشانه افزایش سن نیست، بلکه ممکن است با خطر بیشتر بیماری، افت عملکرد مغز و حتی کاهش امید به زندگی ارتباط داشته باشد. به گفته پژوهشگران، سرعت گام برداشتن بازتابی از عملکرد مجموعه‌ای از دستگاه‌های بدن، از مغز و اعصاب گرفته تا قلب، ریه‌ها، عضلات و استخوان‌هاست. به همین دلیل، برخی دانشمندان آن را یکی از ساده‌ترین و در عین حال موثرترین شاخص‌ها برای ارزیابی سلامت و روند پیری بدن می‌دانند.

items.summary: ابوظبی، امارات متحده عربی — رئیس جمهور دونالد ترامپ، نخست وزیر قطر، شیخ محمد بن عبدالرحمن آل ثانی، روز دوشنبه در کاخ سفید در حالی که تلاش های دیپلماتیک برای پایان دادن به جنگ با ایران ادامه دارد، حتی در شرایطی که مارکو روبیو، وزیر امور خارجه هشدار داد که مذاکرات فاصله زیادی با پیشرفت دارد و تهران نشان می دهد که تمایل به مذاکره برای مذاکره بدون فشار دارد، دیدار کرد. پیام‌های رقابتی در حالی منتشر می‌شوند که تنگه هرمز همچنان منبع اصلی اختلالات اقتصادی جهانی است و دولت‌های منطقه برای راه‌حلی دیپلماتیک برای مناقشه‌ای که کشورهای خلیج‌فارس را در معرض هزاران حمله موشکی و پهپادی ایران قرار داده است، تلاش می‌کنند. روبیو روز یکشنبه قبل از عزیمت به نشست وزرای خارجه گروه 7 در پاریس در گفت و گو با خبرنگاران گفت: پیشرفت اندکی در مذاکرات و رد کردن آن صورت گرفته است.
items.summary_original: ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates — President Donald Trump met Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, on Monday at the White House as diplomatic efforts to end the war with Iran continue, even as Secretary of State Marco Rubio warns that negotiations remain far from a breakthrough and Tehran signals a willingness to negotiate without yielding to pressure. The competing messages come as the Strait of Hormuz remains a major source of global economic disruption and regional governments push for a diplomatic solution to a conflict that has subjected Gulf countries to thousands of Iranian missile and drone attacks . Speaking to reporters Sunday before departing for a G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris, Rubio said there had been little progress in negotiations and rejected the terms put forward by Tehran. "I wouldn't say we're on the verge of a breakthrough," Rubio said. RUBIO DEFENDS TRUMP'S IRAN WAR AS NOT 'NECESSARILY POPULAR, BUT NECESSARY' He emphasized that Trump prefers a diplomatic settlement but described Iran's demands as unrealistic. The 24-year-old suspect had been hospitalized in critical condition since Saturday's shooting in Krakow and underwent several operations before his death. Polish prosecutors have opened an investigation into the killings and attempted killings, including attacks on police officers, as a possible terrorist offense. Authorities said the gunman held far-right views , though investigators have not publicly established a motive for the attack. The three are believed to have died from gunshot wounds, though authorities have not confirmed the circumstances of their deaths. The suspect, who was wearing military-style clothing and a bulletproof vest, drove into Krakow's historic Main Square on Saturday before opening fire, according to authorities. items.summary_original: Israeli President Isaac Herzog announced Saturday that he has chosen opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the country's next government, handing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's chief rival the first opportunity to build a coalition following an inconclusive national election. Herzog announced his decision on Nov. 7, but the formal presentation of the mandate is scheduled for Sunday, Nov. 8, at 5 p.m. Israeli time. Eisenkot will then have 28 days to assemble a government, with a possible 14-day extension. The decision could mark a significant step toward ending Netanyahu’s tenure, but it would also launch a difficult round of coalition negotiations, with deep disagreements among parties seeking to replace him. NETANYAHU DEFIES EXIT POLLS AS VOTE SHIFTS IN HIS FAVOR, BUT MAJORITY REMAINS ELUSIVE Following two days of consultations with Israel’s newly elected parliament, Herzog announced Thursday that factions representing 67 of the Knesset’s 120 members had recommended Eisenkot, chairman of the Yashar party, to form the next government. Netanyahu received the backing of 46 lawmakers, while seven members of the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party declined to endorse either candidate. "The results of the consultations may appear clear," Herzog said in his Nov. 5 statement, but cautioned that competing political demands and vetoes have left the prospects for forming a government uncertain. items.summary_original: Protesters in France are continuing to demonstrate in Paris and across the nation despite police prohibitions on gatherings in the capital. The Paris Police Prefecture denied numerous formal requests for permits allowing protests in various areas of the city, citing October riots that led to thousands of arrests and violent clashes between protesters and law enforcement. "These events demonstrated the intention of certain individuals to target the institutions of the Republic, specifically through actions directed against public buildings and State services in order to undermine the foundations of the Republic," the police wrote, according to a Fox News Digital translation of a police order . "That these elements characterize a particular and serious risk to public institutions, agent safety, and the normal functioning of public services during such demonstrations," the statement continued. items.summary_original: Małopolska Police and MPK S.A. confirmed a Polish gunman opened fire at a popular tourist destination in Kraków Saturday, killing six people and wounding at least 15 more. Of the six dead, four are women and two are men, according to Małopolska Police. Shooting from a moving vehicle, the gunman allegedly targeted people at random, injuring civilians as well as police during the attack on Kraków's bustling Main Square. TEEN WEARING HELMET CAMERA KILLS WORKER AT POLISH SCHOOL AMID FEARS OF COPYCAT ATTACKS "Six people were killed and fifteen were injured in the incident in the Main Market Square, the Małopolska Provincial Office reported. The perpetrator of the attack was shot and detained by police officers. Rescue services are still working at the scene," MPK S.A., the city's municipal public transport company, wrote in a statement shared to X. Video posted on social media showed people running while gunshots rang out. Police shot and wounded the suspect during a gunfight, and the area is now secured, according to authorities. The suspect, who has only been identified by police as a "citizen of the Republic of Poland," was wearing military-style fatigues and used a military-style rifle to carry out the attack, Katarzyna Cisło, a spokesperson for the Kraków police, told Polish network TVN24. "We see some progress. … We hope that both sides will be able to reach a point where they will start building trust and engaging in a way to avoid the war, to find a political solution. … I am a little bit optimistic, but I don't exclude the other option," Dr. Ali Rashid Al Nuaimi, chairman of the Defense, Interior and Foreign Affairs Committee of the UAE's Federal National Council, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview. His remarks came as Reuters reported Nov. 5 that Iran had submitted a new nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar. Tehran, however, continued to insist that the U.S. meet seven conditions before negotiations could proceed, including sanctions relief and an end to the American naval blockade. The opening ceremony of ADIPEC 2026, attended by Fox News Digital, brought together senior government officials and energy industry leaders at a time when the war involving Iran and disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz have placed extraordinary pressure on global energy supplies. But amid discussions about oil production, shipping routes and energy security, Dr. Sultan Al Jaber, the UAE’s minister of industry and advanced technology and chief executive of state-owned energy giant ADNOC, delivered a different challenge to the technology industry. items.summary_original: First lady Melania Trump and envoys from both Russia and Ukraine spoke from the White House on Thursday, hailing the ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Oleshky region as a potential "spark" for peace that lasts beyond a temporary regional ceasefire. "We have chosen humanity over war," the first lady said in a White House trilateral news conference with the two warring countries. "Undeniably, the lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war. I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace. Every significant transformation begins with a small spark." "Together, we can create something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire," she added, calling Oleshky "a spark in a world of darkness capable of illuminating the best in humanity." INSIDE MELANIA TRUMP'S SECRET DIPLOMATIC ROLE IN THE RUSSIA-UKRAINE CEASEFIRE DEAL Trump said she became aware of a humanitarian crisis in the region in September and directed her representative, Marc Beckman, to engage with Russia and Ukraine on her behalf. She said both countries agreed to work with her as an "exclusive intermediary" to establish a ceasefire in Oleshky and the surrounding Kherson region, deliver humanitarian aid and create a safe evacuation route for civilians. Her remarks were followed by comments from Russian special envoy Kirill Dmitriev , who said Russian President Vladimir Putin appreciated President Donald Trump’s efforts to stop the fighting. items.summary_original: France deployed 70,000 police officers Thursday as tens of thousands of people took to the streets for nationwide strikes and protests after left-wing groups called for a mobilization. In Paris, the Eiffel Tower was closed; in Lyon, French riot police fired tear gas and charged a group of protesters; and near Toulouse, a high school was set on fire, according to Reuters. "We need to turn up in big numbers on the streets today," the news agency quoted the head of the left-wing CGT union Sophie Binet as saying. The demonstrations come after France was rocked by violent protests in October, which outgoing French President Emmanuel Macron blamed on "ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic." FRANCE'S MACRON BLAMES PROTESTS ON 'ULTRA-LEFT GROUPS WHOSE AIM IS TO BRING DOWN THE REPUBLIC' An official close to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that by early Thursday, around 270,000 people had joined the union action in 180 rallies outside the capital. About a third of France’s high schools were closed or unable to operate, some because of student blockades and others because teachers were on strike, The Associated Press reported. Toby Harris, an Australian tourist who was visiting Paris on Thursday, told Fox News Digital that "I feel like it's probably a good thing that there's like political action in the city. items.summary_original: Multiple planes across Europe were diverted and forced to make emergency landings Thursday because of bomb threats that have turned out to be unfounded. At least 11 planes, originating from cities including Copenhagen, Dublin, Helsinki, Madrid, Milan and Warsaw, have been affected. The source of the threats was not immediately clear. These incidents came after several flights in Europe received similar warnings on Tuesday that the U.K. government described as "malicious hoax threats." "Upon receiving a threat regarding the placement of an improvised explosive device on board 4 aircraft heading to Prague, we are preparing with colleagues from Prague Airport for their landing. We assess the relevance of the threats as low," Czech Police wrote on X, before adding that inspections of the planes yielded "negative results." The threats come at a time when European officials have been blaming Russia and Iran for "hybrid attacks" and acts of sabotage, which both Moscow and Tehran deny, Reuters reported. Hernandez was participating in fast-rope training at Camp Schwab when he sustained injuries during the training, the 3rd Marine Division said in a later statement to Fox News Digital.
